manufacturer.triumph-adler.description: German maker of office computers, Alphatronic microcomputers, and Dario and Walkstation PCs.
manufacturer.triumph-adler.history:
Triumph’s German bicycle works was founded in Nuremberg in 1896 as a subsidiary of the British company. Adler began making typewriters in Frankfurt towards the end of the nineteenth century. Triumph-Adler’s timeline dates Max Grundig’s purchase of a majority stake in Triumph to 1957, when he brought the two companies together. Their experience with typewriters and office customers paved the way for computing.

The 1968 TA 100 brought electronics to the workstation. The 1971 TA 10 made programming available in a format familiar to small businesses. From 1979 Alphatronic brought the microcomputer to professionals, while Triumph-Adler continued to sell specialised systems. BITSY focused on word processing and the TA 1600 offered configurations for offices with multiple workstations. In 1988 the Unix MSX 3200 range was positioned above the System M32.

Volkswagen took a majority stake in 1979 and sold the company to Olivetti in 1986. During that period, the Dario 286 and 386SX desktops shared a platform with Olivetti’s PCS machines. Triumph-Adler’s timeline dates the Walkstation 286/386 milestone to 1990. That year Olivetti commissioned Triumph-Adler to develop a new portable line. In March 1991 five Nuremberg-built models were announced under both brands.

In 2010 Triumph-Adler and its UTAX brand joined the Kyocera Group. The company that had brought calculation and programming to the desktop went on to specialise in printing and document management.
